title: A formal-meets-empirical slice: empirically testing an ELK-style 'reporter' on a toy model where ground truth is known

original_idea.body:
# A formal-meets-empirical slice: empirically testing an ELK-style 'reporter' on a toy model where ground truth is known

**Problem:** ELK asks how to read what a model 'knows' even when it reports otherwise. Sub-problem: on a small open model where we KNOW the latent fact, does a simple probe-based 'reporter' recover the truth when the model is prompted to lie about it?

**Direction:** Construct a task where the model is given a secret fact and instructed to deny it. Train a probe on activations to recover the true fact despite the deceptive output, and measure how reporter accuracy degrades as deception is made more sophisticated.

**Why it matters:** Grounds an abstract agenda (ELK) in a concrete, beginner-feasible experiment on open weights, single GPU, no training.

**Relevant context:** ARC ELK agenda; honesty/deception probing literature.

low_compute.reasoning: Small open model, probe training only; single GPU.
